entries.content: Using `caveman` skill: terse updates, full technical substance. First read skill, target header, every referenced non-agent file. Then inspect codebase, update only requested feature file, verify diff.

---
name: caveman
description: >
  Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts output tokens 65% (measured) by speaking like caveman
  while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra,
  wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra.
  Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens",
  "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
---

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim â€” unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X â†’ Y) â€” measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully æ–‡è¨€æ–‡. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (ä¹‹/ä¹ƒ/ç‚º/å…¶) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example â€” "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "çµ„ä»¶é »é‡ç¹ªï¼Œä»¥æ¯ç¹ªæ–°ç”Ÿå°è±¡åƒç…§æ•…ã€‚ä»¥ useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹ã€‚"
- wenyan-full: "æ¯ç¹ªæ–°ç”Ÿå°è±¡åƒç…§ï¼Œæ•…é‡ç¹ªï¼›ä»¥ useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹å‰‡å…ã€‚"
- wenyan-ultra: "æ–°åƒç…§å‰‡é‡ç¹ªã€‚useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹ã€‚"

Example â€” "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No per-request handshake."
- wenyan-full: "æ± è“„å·²é–‹ä¹‹é€£ï¼Œä¸é€è«‹è€Œæ–°é–‹ï¼Œçœæ¡æ‰‹ä¹‹è²»ã€‚"
- wenyan-ultra: "æ± è“„é€£ï¼Œå…é€è«‹æ–°é–‹ï¼Œçœæ¡æ‰‹ã€‚"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` â€” order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example â€” destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

FILE: design\feature_descriptions\F_457_add_replace_to_search.md
---
author: 
id: F_457
internalId: 2abaa832-8652-4464-aca4-963549cdbac2
title: add replace to search
status: ready for implementation
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__2abaa832-8652-4464-aca4-963549cdbac2.json
policy:
after: ac32ed09-2e05-4ae3-9a90-8a03bba61616
branch: f_457_add_replace_to_search
worktree: 2
---
In the markdown editor, we have a local search function. We should also include a `replace` feature. So the text that was searched for, can be replaced.

* activated through shortcut ctrl+h. this opens the search box expanded so it also contains the `replace` input
* or if the search box is already open, through a dropdown icon, in front of the search text. when expanded, the user can enter the text that needs to replace the selection.
* user can replace selected text or all at once. there should be a button for this

## Current state

`MarkdownEditor` installs `MarkdownLocalTextSearchPlugin` by default. The action-prompt editor opts out because its containing popup owns `Ctrl+F`. Source mode also hides the local visible-text search control. Toolbarless and read-only rich-text editors keep search through `Ctrl+F`.

The plugin opens a non-blocking popup, submits search only on `Enter` or the Search button, and stores submitted term and case mode separately from draft input. It selects next or previous non-overlapping visible-text match, wraps at document boundaries, reports total matches, and supports matches spanning adjacent Lexical text nodes. Search changes selection only; it does not change Markdown, dirty state, history, or persistence.

No replace input, `Ctrl+H` handler, replacement action, or read-only replacement guard exists. Normal Lexical edits already flow through `MarkdownEditor.handleEditorChange` into draft or data-source editing, dirty state, document history, and existing commit behavior.

## Implementation details

* Define **current match** as match selected by last submitted search or later result navigation. Define **Replace all** as replacing every non-overlapping match present when action starts. Replacement text is literal text and is not searched again during same action; an empty replacement is allowed and deletes matches.
* Add an expand/collapse chevron before search field. This is an expansion control, not a menu. Expanded popup adds replacement input plus accessible `Replace` and `Replace all` buttons. Keep existing find controls and non-blocking `Popper` placement.
* Register `Ctrl+H` in editor-local Lexical keyboard handling. Prevent browser history, open popup expanded, preserve selected-text search seeding, and focus search input. `Ctrl+F` and toolbar search button continue opening find-only state.
* Keep draft find term, submitted find term, replacement text, and current match as separate plugin state. Typing either input must not navigate, replace, or change active result count. Search submission remains required before replacement.
* Extend local-search helper with editor operations that replace current matched Lexical range and all current matches, including matches spanning adjacent text nodes. `Replace all` must process initial matches from document end toward start in one editor update so offset changes cannot skip later matches and one undo restores whole action.
* `Replace` changes only current match, then recalculates remaining count and selects next match from end of inserted text, wrapping when needed. Disable replacement actions when no submitted term exists, no current match exists for `Replace`, or editor is read-only. `Replace all` with zero matches leaves document unchanged.
* Pass `readOnly` through local-search plugin configuration. Read-only editors retain find behavior; expanded replacement fields may be viewed, but mutation buttons remain disabled and no edit occurs.
* Let Lexical updates use existing `MarkdownEditor` change flow. Do not call persistence, dirty-state callbacks, or history stores directly. Successful replacement must serialize Markdown, mark editable document dirty, update its draft or data source, and enter normal undo history.
* Keep case matching, result navigation, selected-text seeding, hidden-toolbar support, overlay ownership, Escape handling, action-prompt opt-out, file search, source mode, and desktop code unchanged.
* Add helper tests for single replacement, cross-node replacement, reverse-order replace-all, deletion, case mode, replacement containing search term, and zero matches. Extend editor tests for expansion controls, `Ctrl+H`, focus, button states, read-only behavior, dirty/data-source changes, result count, selection, and one-step undo for Replace all.

## Acceptance criteria

* `Ctrl+H` inside enabled rich-text Markdown editor prevents browser history and opens local-search popup expanded with focused search input.
* Chevron before search field expands and collapses replacement row. `Ctrl+F` and toolbar search button keep existing find-only opening behavior.
* Expanded row contains accessible replacement input, `Replace`, and `Replace all` controls.
* Typing find or replacement text does not move editor selection or edit document. User must submit find term before replacement actions become available.
* `Replace` changes only current match, updates remaining result count, and selects next remaining match with existing wrap behavior.
* `Replace all` changes every non-overlapping match present when action starts. It handles cross-node matches, does not process matches created by replacement text, and makes no change when count is zero.
* Match-case mode applies to both replacement actions. Empty replacement deletes selected matches.
* Successful replacement follows normal Markdown serialization, dirty-state, draft or data-source update, persistence, and undo flows. Replace all is one undoable action.
* Read-only editors keep search but cannot replace text. Disabled actions cause no Markdown, dirty-state, history, or persistence change.
* Existing next/previous navigation, `F3`, result count, Escape close, non-blocking interaction, sticky placement, hidden-toolbar support, overlay stacking, action-prompt opt-out, and source-mode behavior remain unchanged.

+We should remove this and instead use the default save button on the 'home' tab. When a user edits the diagram, it should, like all other cards and actions and such be saved automatically through the [commit_batcher.ts](app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts)
+
+## Current state
+
+During diagram editing, the Diagram tab shows a separate `DiagramSaveButton`. It calls `DiagramSaveService.save()`, which queues current edited diagram copy and diagram index, then immediately flushes shared commit batch.
+
+Diagram edits already enter normal persistence automatically. `DiagramSaveService` subscribes to model mutations, serializes canonical diagram data, and asks `DiagramViewService` to queue diagram copy and index changes. `DataService.scheduleDiagramCommit()` sends them to `CommitBatcher`, which commits after configured automatic delay. Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` also flush same pending batch through `ProjectPersistenceService`.
+
+`DiagramSaveService.save()` has two other workflow uses: Review dialog saves before closing, and New diagram creation saves dirty current diagram before switching. Those uses protect workflow transitions and are not duplicate toolbar controls.
+
+## Implementation details
+
+* Remove `DiagramSaveButton` from `DiagramMenuTab`, then remove unused button component and its focused component test.
+* Update `DiagramMenuTab` tests to require edit, clipboard, review, metadata, legend, formatting, and comparison controls without a diagram-specific Save/Saved button.
+* Keep automatic model-mutation subscription and existing persistence chain: `DiagramSaveService` queues canonical diagram copy plus diagram index through `DiagramViewService`, `DataService`, and `CommitBatcher`. Do not add direct file writes or another diagram persistence path.
+* Keep `DiagramSaveService.save()` for Review and New diagram transition workflows. Those operations still require an immediate flush before their next step.
+* Keep Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` as manual immediate-flush entry points. Automatic `CommitBatcher` timer remains normal background persistence path.
+* Preserve failure behavior. Queue failures use diagram error dialog; commit failures remain pending, keep edit session dirty, and use project persistence error reporting.
+* Retain service tests proving model mutation queues without explicit Save and acknowledgement occurs only after persistence. Add or adjust menu and project-persistence coverage proving diagram changes enable and flush through shared Commit action.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+* Diagram tab contains no diagram-specific Save or Saved control before, during, or after an edit.
+* Editing diagram automatically queues canonical diagram copy and diagram index in shared `CommitBatcher`; user does not need to open Home tab or press Save first.
+* Queued diagram changes make shared project persistence dirty, enable Home-tab Commit action, and can be flushed with Home Commit or `Ctrl+S`.
+* If user takes no manual action, configured automatic commit delay flushes queued diagram and index changes through normal batch flow.
+* Successful persistence acknowledges saved copy and clears diagram dirty state only for data included in that commit. Edits made during persistence remain dirty and queue again.
+* Commit failure leaves diagram changes pending and editable, with existing user-visible error reporting.
+* Review dialog Save and dirty-diagram handling before New diagram creation still complete immediate persistence before closing or switching diagrams.
+* Cards, actions, other files, diagram Review behavior, diagram creation, commit batching, push behavior, and read-only behavior remain unchanged.
